dimension_justifications.soundness: The finite-pool realized-schedule estimand is coherent, inferential language is appropriately avoided, and the displayed arithmetic checks out. However, every empirical record E10–E15, all implementations, stochastic traces, sampling frames, and analysis code are missing, so none of the central empirical results or the forward-call accounting can be independently verified. Complete outcome disclosure and decision chronology are also absent.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is unusually explicit about its evidence boundary, protocol definitions, contrast orientation, post-selection, missing arm, and limitations. Tables are readable, anonymity holds, the main text is within the nine-page limit, and AI assistance is disclosed. The principal presentation limitation is that some reveal-order tables omit basic arm-level descriptive statistics.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The finite-pool, realized-trace reframing and disciplined organization of protocol contrasts are useful, but the contribution is narrow: no scorer is introduced, no mechanism is isolated, no complete arm comparison is provided, and all empirical values are unverifiable transcriptions from an unavailable source record.

paper_summary: This paper presents an exploratory descriptive audit of multiple-choice scoring protocols for LLaDA-8B-Instruct on constructed GSM8K-MC pools. Five protocols are defined, but outcomes are disclosed for four. The foregrounded n=400 comparison reports s_conf minus mc_uniform of +13.0 percentage points at nominal matched-L draws; a post-selected 2L/2L point also reports +13.0 points, and a 128-draw point reports +9.0 points. On a fresh n=819 pool, s_conf reportedly exceeds one rand_inject realization by 12.58 points, while fixed_inject exceeds s_conf by 5.62 points in aggregate but loses by 12.56 points at answer position 0. The manuscript correctly frames these as finite-pool contrasts conditional on unavailable stochastic realizations and makes no population, causal, stochastic-policy-expectation, or actual-cost claim.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest verifiable contribution is the disciplined estimand and reporting framework. Equation 1 correctly defines a finite-pool, realized-schedule contrast; b, c, and m are consistently oriented; and the printed arithmetic is internally consistent. In particular, all Table 3 differences equal both the accuracy difference and (b-c)/n; the Table 4 pooled difference and discordance count equal the sums across pools; Tables 5–6 reconcile across construction and position strata; and Table 8 counts and reported mean lengths are arithmetically consistent.
strengths: The manuscript clearly distinguishes five source-defined protocols from the four protocols with disclosed outcomes and explicitly identifies anti_inject as missing.
Descriptive and inferential claims are well separated: confidence intervals, tests, and cross-pool inference are omitted because the declared estimand supplies no probability model.
Post-selection is disclosed rather than hidden: the 2L/2L sensitivity, fresh random-order comparison, and position subgroup are labeled post-selected or post-hoc.
The stochastic estimand is carefully bounded to recorded mask draws and reveal schedules, and the paper explicitly denies that a single realization estimates a stochastic-policy expectation.
Whole-protocol contrasts are not misrepresented as component ablations; feedback, masking path, estimator, reveal order, and accounting differences are acknowledged.
The fixed-order heterogeneity is presented with consistent orientation, including the aggregate/position-0 sign reversal and construction-stratified effects.
The PDF is anonymous, visually legible, eight pages total with approximately five main-text pages before references, and includes an author AI-assistance disclosure.
questions: Can the authors provide an anonymous, hashed E10–E15 bundle containing item-level predictions and scores, sampling-frame identifiers, exact prompts and choices, stochastic traces, and aggregation code?

What distinct model invocations constitute the claimed L scoring calls and L selection calls for s_conf? Can selection and the accumulated selected-token loss be obtained from the same forward pass under the stated algorithm?

What is the complete arm × pool × budget × subgroup outcome matrix, including anti_inject, both historical pilots, failed or neutral comparisons, and the chronology by which the displayed rows were selected?
How variable are mc_uniform accuracy and the s_conf–rand_inject contrast across independently reproducible mask streams and reveal schedules?
What are the separate correct counts/accuracies for both arms in Tables 4–6, along with b, c, m, tie counts, exclusions, and missingness?
Can the matched-L comparison be replicated on a genuinely disjoint pool using a frozen protocol and independently generated stochastic realizations?

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract and Evidence notation; p. 3, Sec. 4 and Table 3; pp. 4–5, Sec. 5 and Tables 4–5; p. 5, Sec. 6; Appendix D p. 8, Tables 9–10; experiment_registry.json A14-X1/A14-X2
issues.observed_evidence: The package explicitly states that every empirical value is source-reported and cannot be verified. Table 9 marks every intended evidence object E10–E15 missing. Raw per-item results, pool membership, prompts, choice construction, implementations, model/tokenizer revisions, random draws, reveal schedules, call traces, and analysis code are absent. The manuscript reports that no experiment or analysis was rerun.
issues.why_it_matters: All substantive empirical conclusions depend on records that cannot be inspected, replayed, or recomputed. Internal arithmetic consistency cannot establish that the underlying items, predictions, protocol executions, pairing, or reported accuracies are genuine or correctly labeled. This prevents the empirical contribution from meeting a conference-paper soundness threshold.
issues.required_fix: Release an anonymous hashed experimental bundle with sampling frames, exact model inputs and revisions, all per-item option scores and predictions, protocol code/configurations, tie handling, random-mask draws, reveal orders, call traces, and deterministic aggregation scripts. If historical artifacts cannot be recovered, rerun a frozen protocol and clearly replace unsupported historical results.
issues.verification_test: Validate bundle hashes; reconstruct every choice set and tokenization; replay every disclosed arm; recompute per-arm accuracies, b/c/m counts, strata, and all printed effects; require exact agreement with Tables 1 and 3–8 and document any discrepancy.
issues.evidence_needed: Resolvable E10–E15 artifacts or a new formally frozen experimental bundle with raw records, provenance, and executable recomputation.

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Evidence notation and Sec. 1; p. 2, Sec. 3 and Tables 1–2; p. 3, Table 3; p. 4, Table 4; p. 5, Sec. 5.2 and Sec. 6; experiment_registry.json A14-X1
issues.observed_evidence: The complete evaluated-arm matrix, timestamped registration, hypothesis ledger, and decision chronology are absent. One of five defined arms, anti_inject, has no disclosed outcome. The 2L/2L sensitivity, fresh random-order result, and answer-position analysis are explicitly post-selected or post-hoc. Two historical pilots are mentioned, but only a subset of pool/arm outcomes is displayed.
issues.why_it_matters: Even descriptive estimates can be misleading when arms, pools, budgets, or subgroups are selected after observing results. The current package does not permit assessment of outcome-dependent reporting or multiplicity, and explicit disclosure of this limitation does not restore design completeness.
issues.required_fix: Disclose every evaluated arm, pool, budget, seed, subgroup, exclusion, and analysis, including anti_inject and null or failed runs. Provide a timestamped decision chronology distinguishing prespecified, exploratory, and post-hoc analyses. Foreground results under a prospectively frozen protocol in any new evaluation.
issues.verification_test: Cross-check the disclosed arm × pool × budget × seed matrix and chronology against raw run manifests and timestamps; verify that every completed scientific run has an outcome or a documented non-scientific failure and that headline selection rules were fixed before the new results were observed.
issues.evidence_needed: Complete evaluated-run ledger, arm outcome matrix, registration or immutable protocol timestamp, and decision chronology.

issues.location: PDF pp. 2–3, Sec. 3, especially the finite-pool realized-schedule estimand; p. 4, Sec. 5.1 and Table 4; p. 5, Sec. 6; Appendix A p. 6
issues.observed_evidence: mc_uniform uses one unavailable stored collection of mask draws at each budget, and rand_inject uses one unavailable reveal schedule. The original random schedule reportedly depended on a process-sensitive string hash, so the nominal seed is insufficient for replay. No multi-realization analysis is reported. Equation 1 is internally coherent for a fixed realized record, and the paper appropriately avoids expectation-level claims.
issues.why_it_matters: A single stochastic realization cannot characterize either the mean behavior or stability of a stochastic scoring protocol. Consequently, the reported gaps may be realization-specific, and comparisons across budgets may partly reflect different random streams. The bounded estimand prevents overclaiming but leaves the practical protocol comparison weak.
issues.required_fix: Use a reproducible RNG and evaluate multiple independently generated mask streams and reveal schedules under a frozen protocol. Report the finite-pool contrast for every realization plus descriptive summaries of the realization distribution. Preserve the current realized-trace estimand as a separate, clearly identified object.
issues.verification_test: Recreate every schedule from recorded RNG state; repeat the full evaluation over a justified number of independent realizations; report means, dispersion, ranges or quantiles, and reversal frequencies; verify whether the direction and substantive magnitude of each headline contrast remain stable.
issues.evidence_needed: Persisted RNG states and traces plus multi-realization per-item outputs for mc_uniform and rand_inject.

issues.location: PDF p. 3, Sec. 3, Table 2, and lines 133–135; p. 4, Table 3 and lines 176–182; Appendix C p. 7, Table 7; method_provenance.tsv A14-M4
issues.observed_evidence: The matched-forward-call interpretation assumes s_conf uses L scoring plus L selection calls while mc_uniform at the sensitivity point uses 2L calls. No implementation or instrumented trace supports this ledger. The operational description says that an injected step reads losses, selects a position, and accumulates the selected loss, but does not explain why scoring and selection necessarily require distinct forward passes. This is a cannot_verify concern, not a demonstrated miscount. The paper correctly disclaims FLOP, latency, memory, and energy equality.
issues.why_it_matters: The label 'matched-forward-call-count sensitivity' and its interpretation depend on the 2L ledger. If selection and scoring share a pass, or if calls differ in effective sequence work, the control is mislabeled and does not address the proposed count imbalance even in its narrow stated sense.
issues.required_fix: Specify executable pseudocode and tensor-level call boundaries for every protocol; instrument and release per-candidate call traces; explain whether selected-token loss is obtained during schedule selection or in a separate pass. If 2L is not verified, relabel the row as a 2L-reference-draw operating point and remove the call-matching interpretation or rerun a genuinely count-matched control.
issues.verification_test: Instrument model invocation entry points and compare observed per-candidate counts with L and 2L for every candidate length. Confirm that the same counting unit and batching convention are applied to all arms and reconcile trace totals with Table 7.
issues.evidence_needed: Exact protocol code, pseudocode, instrumentation method, and per-candidate invocation traces.

issues.location: PDF p. 2, Sec. 3 and Table 2; pp. 4–5, Tables 4–5; Appendix B–D pp. 6–8, Tables 6, 8, and 9
issues.observed_evidence: Reveal-order Tables 4–6 do not report both arms' marginal correct counts or accuracies; Table 4 reports only n, rounded contrast, and m rather than explicit b/c; tie and score vectors are absent. anti_inject and the chance-calibration ledger have no outcome. Heterogeneity is shown only for post-hoc construction and answer-position strata of fixed_inject versus s_conf, while the central matched-L comparison is not replicated on the disjoint fresh pool.
issues.why_it_matters: The audit does not provide a complete descriptive picture of absolute performance, ties, arm coverage, or heterogeneity. Aggregate contrasts can conceal low performance or composition effects, and the lack of a disjoint replication leaves the foregrounded result specific to one selected pool and mask realization.
issues.required_fix: Provide a complete arm × pool × budget table with n, correct count, accuracy, b, c, m, ties, exclusions, construction stratum, and answer position. Disclose anti_inject and calibration outcomes. Replicate the foregrounded matched-L comparison on an independently constructed disjoint pool and report all prespecified strata.
issues.verification_test: Recompute every marginal and paired statistic from item-level records; confirm that b-c equals the difference in correct counts and that stratum counts aggregate exactly. Verify pool disjointness by item identifiers and rerun the frozen matched-L protocol on the new pool.
issues.evidence_needed: Complete item-level outcome matrix, tie fields, E15 calibration record, anti_inject outcomes, and a disjoint matched-L replication.

issues.location: PDF p. 2, Sec. 2; Appendix E p. 8; citation_lock.json
issues.observed_evidence: The closest scoring mechanism and three adjacent sources have a primary-source lock, and the novelty boundary is cautiously phrased. However, the manuscript and citation lock state that the bibliography-wide metadata and sentence-support audit is incomplete; Cobbe et al. is not included in the supplied verified entries.
issues.why_it_matters: The narrow novelty claim is reasonably bounded, but a complete citation check is needed before asserting that the positioning and benchmark provenance are fully verified.
issues.required_fix: Verify every remaining bibliography entry and each local support claim against primary sources, then update the citation lock without broadening novelty language beyond verified coverage.
issues.verification_test: For each citation, match title, authors, year, venue, and identifier to the primary source and record the exact manuscript sentence it supports; confirm that no uncited broader novelty assertion remains.
issues.evidence_needed: Completed primary-source citation lock covering all bibliography entries and local claims.

ethics_concerns: No material ethics issue is evident from the frozen submission. The work evaluates an existing model on a constructed benchmark and does not report human-subject data. The manuscript responsibly limits its claims and discloses AI assistance. Any future artifact release should still avoid exposing confidential benchmark annotations or identifying metadata if such material exists.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by a fresh, isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. It had read-only access only to the frozen round-2 snapshot, did not inspect prior rounds or parent directories, and did not use the internet.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A replayable anonymous E10–E15 bundle whose recomputed item-level results exactly reproduce all reported accuracies, b/c/m counts, strata, and candidate-length summaries.
A complete evaluated-arm and hypothesis ledger showing all arms, pools, budgets, seeds, subgroups, failures, and chronological selection decisions, including anti_inject.
Prospectively frozen multi-realization evaluations showing that mc_uniform and rand_inject conclusions are stable across reproducible random streams.
A disjoint-pool replication of the matched-L comparison with complete descriptive statistics and no outcome-dependent exclusions.
Instrumented traces establishing the exact s_conf call accounting and validating the narrow 2L/2L matching claim.
A completed primary-source citation audit confirming the restrained closest-work and novelty boundary.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Replay of the recovered records fails to reproduce any central accuracy, discordance count, pool size, or subgroup effect.
The complete arm matrix reveals omitted evaluated arms, pools, budgets, or seeds with materially conflicting outcomes.
Multi-realization evaluation shows frequent sign reversals or that the reported stochastic realization was an outlier.
Sampling-frame inspection reveals overlap between purportedly disjoint pools, construction leakage, duplicates, or outcome-dependent exclusions.
Instrumentation shows that s_conf does not use the claimed 2L forward calls or that counting conventions differ across arms.
Primary-source checking shows that prior work already contains the purported protocol-audit contribution or that a cited source does not support its local statement.
review_limitations: By instruction, the review was restricted to the frozen snapshot and could not inspect the unavailable source manuscript, raw artifacts, implementation, earlier reviews, repository history, or internet sources.
Empirical authenticity and citation completeness therefore remain cannot_verify rather than demonstrated errors.
The budget-accounting concern identifies an unresolved ambiguity; the supplied evidence is insufficient to prove that the reported 2L count is wrong.
